source.role: English objective and progression anchors only; Japanese scenes are original and Spanish currency, foods, and grammar are not copied

lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Say breakfast words clearly and greet a server or barista politely in the morning.
lessons.title: Morning at the café
lessons.objective: Greet café staff politely, say your name, and recognize common breakfast words in hiragana and katakana.
lessons.focus: おはようございます is a polite morning greeting. は in わたしは is pronounced wa; です makes a polite statement. Long vowels matter in コーヒー. Katakana often marks loanwords such as コーヒー and メニュー.
lessons.scene: Sam enters a small café in the morning and asks about breakfast.

cards.note: Often written お茶; introduced in kana first.

cards.ja: ありがとうございます
よろしくおねがいします
cards.note: Contextual greeting, not a word-for-word equivalent.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: サムさん、よろしくおねがいします。

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: メニューはありますか。

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: コーヒーとパンはありますか。
reader.en: Do you have coffee and bread?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。

speaking.opening: おはようございます。ご注文は何になさいますか。
speaking.goal: Greet the staff, say your name, and ask whether coffee and bread are available.
speaking.closure: Thank the staff politely; do not claim an order was placed unless it was confirmed.

modes.type: Type コーヒー and メニュー from English cues with kana help.
modes.say: Greet the café worker and ask about coffee and bread.
modes.write: Write a polite two-line greeting and menu question.

lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Use numbers, prices in pesos, clock times and café quantities to order and check a total.
lessons.title: Two coffees and the total
lessons.objective: Order two coffees and three pieces of bread using Japanese counters, then confirm a price in yen.
lessons.focus: Use コーヒーを二はい for two cups and パンを三つ for three general pieces. ですか asks for confirmation. 円 means yen; café prices vary, so the example total is fictional. The Spanish source's pesos are intentionally adapted to yen.
lessons.scene: Sam and a friend order at a café counter and check the stated total.

reader.speaker: Sam

speaking.goal: Order two coffees and three pieces of bread; ask for and repeat the total in yen.
speaking.closure: Only confirm the price the partner actually states.

lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Describe food, drinks and tables at a café with ser and estar.
lessons.title: A table and a hot coffee
lessons.objective: Ask whether a table is available and describe the temperature or taste of a drink or food without importing Spanish ser/estar grammar.
lessons.focus: Use この席は空いていますか to ask about seat availability. あつい describes a hot drink; つめたい describes a cold one. Japanese adjectives do not map onto the Spanish ser/estar distinction, so this lesson teaches predicate adjectives and current-state expressions instead.
lessons.scene: Sam asks for a table, then checks a coffee and a sweet pastry with the server.

cards.ja: この席は空いていますか
コーヒーはあついです

reader.en: Excuse me. Is this seat available?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、空いています。どうぞ。
reader.en: Yes, it is available. Please go ahead.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: このコーヒーはあついですね。
reader.en: This coffee is hot, isn't it?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: このパンはあまいですか。

speaking.opening: いらっしゃいませ。お席をお探しですか。
speaking.goal: Ask whether a seat is free and describe whether your coffee is hot and bread is sweet.
speaking.closure: Thank the staff; avoid claiming any allergy accommodation.
